ShortDescription.Value: Fixes the tourism simulation: arrivals by plane and ferry, demand that scales with city size, real length of stay, and honest numbers.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Tourism Overhaul
Cities: Skylines II ships tourism with several defects that make the feature feel inert. This mod fixes them at the simulation level. Every change was derived by tracing the game's own assemblies; nothing here is guesswork.
## What it fixes
**Arrivals are no longer thrown away.** The base game assigns each tourist a single transport mode by one random roll — 10% road, 10% train, 50% air, 30% sea — then looks for an outside connection of exactly that type. If none exists it gives up with no fallback, but still creates the tourist household without a location. That household can never be given citizens, so it is quietly deleted. On a city with no airport and no harbour, 80% of all tourist arrivals are destroyed this way. This mod redistributes the share across the connection types your city actually has, and keeps the intended preference for planes and ferries once you build an airport or harbour.
**Tourism scales with your city.** The base game targets `attractiveness x 15` tourists, and attractiveness is itself capped at 100 — a flat 1,500 tourists no matter how large or attractive the city becomes. This mod scales the target with population.
**Tourists have a real length of stay.** The game declares and saves a tourist departure timer, and a function that returns a stay length, but never calls either. This mod implements the mechanic using the field the game already has.
**The numbers mean something.** The tourism panel computes a figure roughly eight times larger than the game can ever produce, and undercounts tourists who are travelling between destinations. This mod reports the real values.
## Compatibility
No Harmony patches, no reflection, no disabled native systems. Arrivals use real outside connections, real vehicles, real pathfinding, real hotels and the real economy. Safe to add to and remove from an existing save.
Everything is toggleable and tunable in the settings panel.
